grades: Apply as a high school freshman (grade 9)
name: STEM Scholars, The Franklin Institute
what_you_do: This is a free four-year STEM program. It starts in 9th grade. Each year has STEM programming. Rising seniors are paid for a 10-week lab research experience.
who_can_apply: Students living in Philadelphia and surrounding areas who are entering 9th grade, interested in STEM, able to commit to four years, with a 3.0 GPA (per FAQ). Non-freshmen are rarely accepted.
pay_detail: Free to students; rising seniors are paid for lab research (rate not stated). Fees covered by donors.
duration: Four years, grades 9 to 12; research window of 10 weeks between late June and early September
deadline_text: Applications for the next freshman cohort are currently closed; check back for the 2027 class. FAQ says applications usually open late September or early October and are due mid-December.
how_to_apply: Online application, essay, transcript, two recommendation letters, then an interview with Youth Programs staff.
notes: The FAQ timing and the 'currently closed' message are not fully consistent, so confirm on the page. The sister middle-school program PACTS is for grades 6 to 8.
